variants.note: Craftsman's own defining_characteristics #1: 'Low-pitched gabled roof, front- or side-facing.'
Prairie's device, not Craftsman's; see the parent family's own roof_form note on the split.

roof_form.rule: The principal roof is gabled, front- or side-facing, low-pitched.
roof_form.note: Overrides the parent's deliberately-open gable/hip split with Craftsman's own documented answer, stopping the cascade here rather than letting it reach either the parent's open pairing or any distant ancestor.

roof_pitch.rule: Principal roof pitch between 3:12 and 6:12 (own hard constraint c03).
roof_pitch.note: Restates the node's own hard constraint c03 directly; the parent's identical 3:12-6:12 band already resolves this correctly, but this node's own constraint is the more specific and more authoritative source.

projection_in.note: Own hard constraint c01: eave and rake overhang 24-36 in, equal on eave and rake within 6 in; an overhang under 18 in disqualifies the node.

eave_condition.rule: Eave and rake overhang shall be between 24 and 36 in, and shall be equal on eave and rake within 6 in (own hard constraint c01).
eave_condition.note: Narrows the parent's shared 24-48 in family band to Craftsman's own tighter, hard-constrained figure, and resolves the parent's own open gable/hip branch point down to the exposed-rafter-tails answer Craftsman alone canonically takes.

gable_treatment.rule: The gable is built of an exposed truss with a projecting purlin running through the gable-end wall, a knee brace under the overhang, and (in high-craft work) a shaped and rounded beam end -- the Swiss chalet and Japanese-timber inheritances made visible.
gable_treatment.note: Directly grounded in defining_characteristics #2 and the node's own long description of its Swiss-chalet and Japanese parents' contributions (exposed purlin, projecting ridge beam, knee brace, shaped beam end).

chimney.rule: The chimney is faced in river boulder, arroyo stone, or over-fired clinker brick, laid deliberately irregular against the regular woodwork, and is expressed as a solid mass rather than a decorative accent.
chimney.note: Directly grounded in the node's own diagnostic_tells: 'River boulder, arroyo stone, or over-fired clinker brick used for chimney, porch base, and foundation -- deliberately irregular masonry against regular woodwork.'

wing_strategy.rule: The house is a single dominant volume rather than an additive assembly of wings; where a wing occurs it is subordinate in ridge height, consistent with the one-to-one-and-a-half-storey norm.
wing_strategy.note: Not stated directly by the node; inferred from its own massing_affinities (bungalow-linear canonical, gable-front-and-wing only 'possible') and the general absence of any additive-growth discussion in its own text (contrast with american-farmhouse-vernacular, whose whole identity is additive growth).

primary_cladding.rule: Cladding stacks base to top -- stone or clinker brick base, shingle or clapboard middle, stucco or shingle gable -- with each change at a structural line (material_change_rule, family level).
primary_cladding.note: Grounded in defining_characteristics #5 ('Stacked natural materials expressing base, wall, and gable, with each transition at a structural line').

foundation_expression.rule: The foundation is exposed rough masonry -- river boulder, arroyo stone, or clinker brick -- matching the chimney and porch base, not a smooth poured skirt.
foundation_expression.note: Same source as chimney, above: the node's own diagnostic tell names foundation alongside chimney and porch base.

window_proportion.rule: Upper sash divided into three or four vertical lights; lower sash undivided -- a vertical division within a sash whose overall proportion is set by the storey, not by a wide horizontal ratio.
window_proportion.note: CASCADE FIX. Before this binding, the slot resolved a Tudor-derived 'wide rather than tall... horizontal multi-light grid' proportion from tudor-jacobean -- the opposite of a double-hung sash's own vertical proportion, and inconsistent with window_type (already fixed on this node to double-hung, forbidding casement-leaded). Grounded in the node's own typical_ratios: 'Upper sash divided into three or four vertical lights; lower sash undivided.'

window_head_wood.rule: The window head is a flat, wide casing, unmoulded, sharing the datum of every other window and door head on the storey (see own proportional_system: 'window and door heads at 6 ft 8 in to 7 ft 0 in on a single datum').

window_sill.rule: The sill is a plain projecting wood member sized like the casing, not a moulded classical sill.

variants.note: A detached single- or double-bay garage at the rear of the lot, trimmed in the same wide-board vocabulary and roofed to match the house, reached by a driveway along one side.
Set back from the principal facade plane and subordinate in height, its door never on the entrance elevation.
A garage door on the entrance elevation defeats the porch-forward composition this style depends on.

garage_strategy.rule: The garage is a subordinate volume, ideally detached at the rear of the lot; where attached, it is recessed behind the principal facade plane and its door is never on the entrance elevation.
garage_strategy.note: No historical precedent exists for this slot (garage_strategy, per docs/inheritance.md), so this is authored rather than retrieved, per docs/inheritance.md's own guidance that the slot 'should be specified on every contemporary buildable variant.' Craftsman remains one of the most commonly built-anew styles in this family today, which is the basis for specifying it here rather than leaving it open.

porch_type.rule: The porch roof must be framed under the primary roof -- either as a continuation of the main slope or as a subordinate gable tied into it. A shed roof applied to the wall below the main eave is forbidden (own hard constraint c02).

porch_depth.rule: Porch depth 7 to 9 ft clear; porch width not less than 60 percent of the facade.
porch_depth.note: Directly from the node's own typical_ratios.

porch_support.rule: Porch supports must be square posts or battered piers on masonry bases not less than 24 in wide (own hard constraint c04); base width 24 to 36 in, tapering to 12 to 18 in at the beam.

trim_family.rule_append: The picture rail sits at door-head datum and the casing family is three boards: a 1x4 leg, a 1x6 head, and a 1x8 base, per the node's own bound trim-craftsman pack.
trim_family.note: Extends the family's own trim_family binding with Craftsman's own more specific three-board casing figure (already cited in the node's own proportion_packs note for trim-craftsman).

casing.rule: Casing is a three-board family: a 1x4 leg, a 1x6 head, and a 1x8 base, per the node's own bound trim-craftsman pack.
casing.note: Overrides the parent's generic 4-5 in casing width with Craftsman's own more specific three-board schedule.

circulation_parti.rule_append: The front door opens directly into the living room with no vestibule in the small plan-book examples, and the kitchen moves close to the dining space with a built-in buffet replacing the sideboard -- a servantless-household plan.
circulation_parti.note: Extends the family's own open-plan rule with Craftsman's own specific evidence for it, drawn from its own long description.

hearth_position.rule: The hearth sits on an interior wall of the living room and is the room's organizing object; built-in bookcases flank it (built_ins, family level).

body_width_ft.note: Craftsman Bungalow's own typical_ratios; carried up to the parent style as its dominant expression.

depth_and_pile.rule: Single-pile to shallow double-pile depending on plan size; the bungalow-linear massing (canonical) is fundamentally a single-loaded plan.

orientation_rule.rule: The porch elevation faces the street or the principal approach; beyond that, orientation is set by site and sun rather than by a fixed compass rule.
